category_law: Negative cases executed against synthetic carriers only. A refusal here demonstrates the guard mechanism fires on synthetic input; it does not demonstrate governance of any real source.
principle_under_test: A ceiling must be able to stop an operation BEFORE it occurs, not merely report it afterwards.

cases.name: read-count ceiling
cases.strength: The denied read never reached the underlying file. The compiled reader observed a short read and failed rather than continuing.

cases.name: byte ceiling
cases.assertion: the read that would have crossed the byte ceiling did not execute
cases.stated_granularity: Bytes delivered may exceed the byte maximum by at most the size of one in-flight read, because the ceiling is evaluated before each read rather than mid-read. Observed overshoot here was 7 bytes on a 16-byte ceiling.
cases.honest_limitation: This is a pre-read gate, not a hard byte-exact cut. A byte-exact ceiling would require the broker to truncate the returned buffer, which would corrupt the stream and is not proposed.

cases.name: no refusal when under ceiling
cases.assertion: the guard does not fire spuriously
cases.why_this_matters: A guard that always fires would be useless. Confirmed inert when no ceiling is set.

cases.name: refusal propagates to the caller rather than being swallowed
cases.assertion: a refused read cannot degrade into a silently truncated decode

cases.name: reused-broker chunked DTA is refused by the format, not silently mis-decoded

setup.condition: one broker reused across successive row_offset chunk parses

cases.assertion: the chunked DTA failure mode is loud, not silent
cases.note: This is a correctness finding as much as a negative case: the failure is detectable, which is why defect D1 in 07 is safe to detect in testing.

not_exercised: An open-count ceiling was implemented but not exercised as a negative case; it is listed as available in the design.
Any ceiling against a real source. Out of authority and not attempted.
